Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, particularly Articles 3–4; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May implementing Law 10/2010; and Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales, RCTIR). The general beneficial-owner test is a natural person holding, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of the capital or voting rights, or otherwise exercising control; where none is identified, the senior managing official is recorded under the statutory fallback. Companies must obtain, maintain, and update beneficial-ownership information and provide it to competent authorities and obliged entities. Access to the RCTIR is governed by applicable law and is not unrestricted public access.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

An SL must have a registered office in Spain under the Spanish Companies Act (Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010). A virtual-office address is not categorically prohibited if it is a genuine, legally usable registered-office address and satisfies registry, tax, and service-of-process requirements. For wholesale semiconductor trading, a virtual office alone may be inadequate for banking onboarding, tax residence and substance evidence, inventory operations, customs records, or counterparties' due diligence. Document actual decision-making, personnel, contracts, accounting, inventory or third-party logistics arrangements, and the authority to use the address.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

The competent Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office; the Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) issues the company-name clearance certificate.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), including Articles 4 (minimum capital), 20–23 (formation and articles), 31–33 (execution and effectiveness of incorporation), and 62–63 (capital contributions). Law 14/2013 of 27 September and applicable implementing rules govern electronic formation through CIRCE.

Formation / constitutional filings

Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), filed for registration in the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 43 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

The statutory minimum share capital for an SL is EUR 1. Contributions must be fully assumed and paid at formation. Until share capital reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to legal reserve, and shareholders are jointly and severally liable for the difference between EUR 3,000 and subscribed capital if the company is liquidated with insufficient assets. No statutory escrow account is required. A bank certificate may evidence cash contributions; non-cash contributions require a description and valuation in the deed.

Funding & unlock path: No general national pre-operation civil-defence certificate applies solely to wholesale trading. The premises must satisfy applicable building, fire-safety, accessibility, and occupational-risk requirements; municipal activity procedures may require a competent technical certificate or project, fire-safety documentation, and structural or load verification based on the premises and stored goods. Employers must comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention and implementing rules.

Paid-in capital rule: The statutory minimum share capital for an SL is EUR 1. Contributions must be fully assumed and paid at formation. Until share capital reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to legal reserve, and shareholders are jointly and severally liable for the difference between EUR 3,000 and subscribed capital if the company is liquidated with insufficient assets. No statutory escrow account is required. A bank certificate may evidence cash contributions; non-cash contributions require a description and valuation in the deed.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscriptions set out in the incorporation deed and confirms that the subscribed shares have been fully paid as stated therein. RESOLVED, that the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted, subject to registration and any required shareholder approval. RESOLVED, that [name and identification number] is appointed [sole director/joint directors/board member] and [name] is appointed [managing director/secretary], each subject to the articles and applicable law. RESOLVED, that the appointed officers are authorized to obtain the Company’s tax identification number, complete tax and registry formalities, open operating bank accounts, and make required commercial and administrative registrations.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Exempted / Not Required

No national industrial licensing board approval is generally required for wholesale brokerage of SSDs and server processors without manufacturing or regulated industrial processes. The competent municipal authority governs premises activity and works formalities; the relevant Autonomous Community industrial authority applies only if a regulated installation or industrial activity is introduced.

Category: No specific national manufacturing or industrial operating permit generally applies. A premises-specific municipal responsible declaration (declaración responsable), prior communication (comunicación previa), or activity licence may be required, depending on the municipality, premises, and activity.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT. The AEAT administers the Spanish Tax Identification Number (NIF), Corporate Income Tax, Value Added Tax, Intrastat and related registration obligations.

E-government filing portal

A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a definitive NIF from the AEAT after incorporation and registration with the Commercial Registry. The incorporation file normally includes the public deed, articles of association, Commercial Registry evidence, registered office, corporate purpose, identification of directors and beneficial owners, and powers of attorney where applicable. A provisional NIF may be requested during formation using Form 036, followed by submission of the definitive registration evidence. Foreign shareholders, directors and authorized representatives generally require Spanish NIFs for tax and corporate filings; non-resident individuals commonly obtain an NIE, while non-resident legal entities obtain an NIF through the AEAT using Form 036 and supporting constitutional, tax-residence and representation documents. The company must file Form 036 to register in the census of entrepreneurs, professionals and withholding agents, state its VAT activities and communicate its tax address. For intra-Community acquisitions or supplies, the company must request registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and obtain an ES-prefixed VAT identification number. VIES validation should be completed before applying intra-Community exemptions. Electronic filing generally requires an AEAT digital certificate or an authorized representative.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a definitive NIF from the AEAT after incorporation and registration with the Commercial Registry. The incorporation file normally includes the public deed, articles of association, Commercial Registry evidence, registered office, corporate purpose, identification of directors and beneficial owners, and powers of attorney where applicable. A provisional NIF may be requested during formation using Form 036, followed by submission of the definitive registration evidence. Foreign shareholders, directors and authorized representatives generally require Spanish NIFs for tax and corporate filings; non-resident individuals commonly obtain an NIE, while non-resident legal entities obtain an NIF through the AEAT using Form 036 and supporting constitutional, tax-residence and representation documents. The company must file Form 036 to register in the census of entrepreneurs, professionals and withholding agents, state its VAT activities and communicate its tax address. For intra-Community acquisitions or supplies, the company must request registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and obtain an ES-prefixed VAT identification number. VIES validation should be completed before applying intra-Community exemptions. Electronic filing generally requires an AEAT digital certificate or an authorized representative.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

A Spanish SL is generally subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal taxpayer; Spain does not provide a general United States-style check-the-box election for an SL to elect transparent or disregarded treatment. Tax consolidation may be elected by qualifying Spanish-resident companies and qualifying permanent establishments within a group, subject to statutory ownership, control, filing and timing conditions. The company may also access specific statutory regimes, including the special regime for newly created entities where applicable, the reduced-size-entity regime where applicable, and other sector-specific or restructuring regimes. Spanish anti-hybrid mismatch rules implementing ATAD II apply by operation of law and are not elective. The tax treatment of a foreign-owned SL may also be affected by controlled foreign company, transfer pricing, beneficial ownership, withholding tax and treaty rules.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general domestic VAT turnover threshold applies in Spain. A business carrying out taxable supplies in the Spanish VAT territory must register and comply from the commencement of the relevant economic activity or taxable transaction, subject to applicable exemptions and special regimes. The €85,000 EU SME exemption threshold is not currently a general Spanish domestic registration threshold. Separate registration may be required for intra-Community transactions, imports, distance sales, marketplaces, warehousing or other cross-border activities.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods dispatched or transported from the Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with a right of deduction under the Spanish VAT Law, provided the seller or an authorized intermediary can substantiate the export and the goods actually leave the EU customs territory. The claim requires a valid customs export declaration and reliable evidence of exit, linked to the commercial invoice and transport documentation. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for VAT exemption rather than domestic zero-rating where the goods are transported to another EU Member State, the customer has a valid VAT identification number in another Member State, the supplier verifies and reports the transaction, and the transport and recapitulative-statement requirements are satisfied. Services supplied to non-EU customers are not automatically zero-rated; the place-of-supply rules must be applied. B2B services are commonly taxed where the customer is established and may be outside Spanish VAT, while specific use-and-enjoyment, immovable-property, passenger transport, admission, intermediary and other special rules can override the general rule. Input VAT refunds are generally claimed through periodic VAT returns by established businesses. Non-established businesses use the applicable refund procedure, including the EU electronic refund mechanism or the non-EU procedure under the statutory reciprocity and other eligibility conditions.

  • Electronic Export Administrative Document or equivalent export customs declaration, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
  • AEAT or EU customs release and exit confirmation, such as the electronic exit result or equivalent proof that the goods left the EU customs territory
  • Commercial invoice identifying the seller, buyer, goods, value, delivery terms and export transaction
  • Packing list and product description sufficient to reconcile the shipment with the customs declaration
  • Bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note or other transport document
  • Purchase order, sales contract and delivery or acceptance evidence where required to establish the transaction chain
  • Evidence linking the customs declaration, transport document, invoice, goods and recipient
  • Import clearance or destination-country customs evidence where relevant and commercially available
  • Payment records or bank evidence where relevant to substantiate the underlying supply; a Spanish inward-remittance certificate is not a general statutory prerequisite for VAT export exemption
  • For intra-Community supplies: customer VAT identification evidence, transport proof to the other Member State, and accurate EC Sales List reporting

Spanish invoices must satisfy formal requirements, including issuer and customer identification, NIF or VAT number where required, invoice number and date, description, taxable base, VAT rate and amount, and applicable exemption or reverse-charge wording. The Immediate Supply of Information system (Suministro Inmediato de Información, or SII) requires qualifying taxpayers, including businesses exceeding the applicable turnover threshold, VAT groups and REDEME registrants, to electronically transmit specified invoice-register data to the AEAT generally within four business days, subject to statutory adjustments. SII is a transaction-data reporting system and is not a universal real-time pre-clearance requirement for all businesses. Spain's Law 18/2022 on business creation and growth establishes phased B2B electronic invoicing obligations, whose operative timing depends on implementing regulations. Royal Decree 1007/2023 establishes technical requirements for computerized invoicing systems and the VERI*FACTU framework, with implementation deadlines subject to the applicable transitional rules and subsequent amendments. Electronic records must preserve integrity, authenticity, traceability and auditability; unauthorized alteration, omission or destruction can trigger tax penalties. Electronic customs declarations are submitted through the AEAT customs systems and the EU customs platform.

Spain has no general rule requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days as a condition for VAT export exemption. Export VAT treatment depends principally on proof of dispatch or transport outside the EU and customs exit, not on a fixed foreign-exchange repatriation period. The AEAT may deny or claw back the exemption and assess unpaid VAT, late-payment interest and applicable penalties where export conditions are not met, exit cannot be evidenced, documents are inconsistent, goods were diverted to the Spanish or EU market, or the transaction is fictitious. Tax penalties may be imposed for incorrect or incomplete tax returns, failure to issue compliant invoices, obstruction of inspection, inaccurate customs declarations and fraudulent conduct. Serious or intentional cases may involve enhanced penalties, customs debt, seizure or forfeiture measures, and criminal tax or customs exposure where statutory thresholds and intent requirements are met. A voluntary correction before formal inspection may reduce exposure under applicable Spanish penalty rules; documentary retention and consistent reconciliation of invoices, customs records, transport evidence, inventory and payment records are essential.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Full convertibility is guaranteed for both current and capital account transactions under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Spanish Law 19/2003 on capital movements. No prior administrative authorization is required for inward equity injections, trade remittances, loan repayments, or profit distributions. The only substantive compliance gates are (i) balance-of-payments statistical declarations (S-1/S-2 forms) for transactions with non-residents exceeding EUR 50,000, (ii) AML/CFT and sanctions screening, and (iii) tax withholding procedures. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted, subject only to corporate income tax settlement and, where applicable, the non-resident income tax withholding return (form 216) at the applicable double tax treaty rate (generally 10-15% for treaty jurisdictions and 19% for non-treaty jurisdictions). There are no dividend quotas, remittance licenses, or reinvestment obligations.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation, or conversion regime for export proceeds. A Spanish exporter may freely hold, in EUR or any foreign currency, the proceeds from sales of goods or services. The only statutory requirement is declaratory: transactions with non-resident counterparties equal to or exceeding EUR 50,000 (or cumulative quarterly thresholds) must be submitted to the Banco de España via the S-1 statistical declaration within the month following the operation, classifying the transaction under the balance-of-payments goods code. No conversion ratio or sales foreign-exchange timeline applies.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the European System of Central Banks and the Single Supervisory Mechanism, together with the Secretaría General del Tesoro y Financiación Internacional of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation as the competent authorities for balance-of-payments statistics and external transactions reporting. Spain has no separate foreign exchange administration agency; the Bank of Spain supervises all resident credit institutions and authorized electronic money institutions.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% on distributions made to non-resident shareholders under the general non-resident income tax regime (IRNR). The Spanish SL is obligated to withhold and remit the 19% withholding when distributing dividends to a non-resident beneficial owner that is not resident in an EU member state or a jurisdiction with a DTA. Dividends distributed to EU parent companies may qualify for the Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption at 0% if the shareholder holds at least 5% of the capital (or a 5% voting right alternative) for at least one year, subject to anti-abuse rules.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year (i.e., for a 31 December year-end, filing deadline is 25 July of the following year). Actual tax year may differ if the company was newly incorporated (first tax period may exceed 12 months). The tax return must be filed within 25 days after the end of the statutory six-month filing window; payment of the resulting tax liability is due simultaneously with the return.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 00001 (Identificación del contribuyente) Tax identification number (NIF), corporate name, and registered address of the entity. Spanish SL with non-resident shareholders must provide the entity NIF; each non-resident shareholder must maintain a Spanish tax representative if they engage in Spanish-source activities. The return is filed at entity level; non-resident ownership details are not entered on Modelo 200 but are disclosed through corresponding information returns (Modelo 232, Modelo 296). Late filing penalty of 1% of the tax payable plus an additional 1% for each full month of delay; if the return is filed without payment, a surcharge of 20% of the tax amount (apremio reducido) may apply if settled within specified voluntary periods. Failure to file within the statutory deadline may trigger a flat penalty of EUR 200 plus EUR 20 per month of delay for entities with a tax base above EUR 3,000, or EUR 150 plus EUR 15 per month for smaller entities. Where the tax authority formally requires filing after non-submission, the penalty is 50% of the tax base or between EUR 1,500 and EUR 20,000 depending on the type of omission. Interest de demora accrues at the statutory rate (currently 3.75% for 2025). Incorrect filing resulting in non-payment may be classified as an infracción leve (fine of 50% of the unpaid amount, reduced to 25% upon conformity) or grave (50%-100%).
Box 00124 / Box 00125 (Base imponible) Taxable base before offset of prior-year tax losses. Computed from accounting profit adjusted by permanent and temporary differences. The SL must determine Spanish-source taxable income on a worldwide basis in its capacity as a resident entity. For non-resident parent or group entities, transfer pricing adjustments must be reflected in the taxable base in accordance with the arm's length principle; documentation supporting the adjustment must be retained. Late filing penalty of 1% of the tax payable plus an additional 1% for each full month of delay; if the return is filed without payment, a surcharge of 20% of the tax amount (apremio reducido) may apply if settled within specified voluntary periods. Box 00130 (Compensación de bases imponibles negativas) Offset of prior-year tax losses carried forward, capped at 70% of the taxable base for large taxpayers (turnover above EUR 20 million), 25% for taxpayers with turnover between EUR 1 million and EUR 20 million, and 50% for entities under the reduced-size regime, with a statutory carryforward period of 5 years. Losses utilized must be reconciled with the 5-year carryforward records. Non-resident shareholders cannot claim the entity's losses. Any loss-offset adjustment affecting the participation value of non-resident ownership is outside the corporate return's field scope. Late filing penalty of 1% of the tax payable plus an additional 1% for each full month of delay; if the return is filed without payment, a surcharge of 20% of the tax amount (apremio reducido) may apply if settled within specified voluntary periods. Incorrect filing resulting in non-payment may be classified as an infracción leve (fine of 50% of the unpaid amount, reduced to 25% upon conformity) or grave (50%-100%).
Box 00274 (Tipo de gravamen) Applicable tax rate. General rate 25%; reduced-size entities 20%; new entities first two profitable years 15%; certain cooperative entities 20%; entities dedicated to oil exploration or production 48% for the 2023-2025 period. For a wholesale distribution SL, apply the general rate of 25% unless the entity qualifies as a reduced-size entity (turnover below EUR 1 million) or a newly created entity in its first two profitable tax periods. Non-resident shareholders do not apply their own rate to the corporate return. Late filing penalty of 1% of the tax payable plus an additional 1% for each full month of delay; if the return is filed without payment, a surcharge of 20% of the tax amount (apremio reducido) may apply if settled within specified voluntary periods. Box 00582 (Deducciones por doble imposición internacional) International double taxation relief: deduction for taxes paid abroad on income sourced and taxed in foreign countries; deduction for dividends or profits distributed by a foreign entity when double taxation arises. When the Spanish SL receives dividends, interest, or royalties from non-resident related or unrelated parties, the foreign withholding tax may be credited against the Spanish corporate income tax liability subject to the applicable DTA network and the limits of Article 31 of the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law (LIS). Supporting certificates of foreign tax payment must be submitted with the tax records. Incorrect filing resulting in non-payment may be classified as an infracción leve (fine of 50% of the unpaid amount, reduced to 25% upon conformity) or grave (50%-100%).
Box 00600 (Deducción para evitar la doble imposición económica: dividendos y plusvalías de fuente interna) Domestic economic double taxation relief for dividends and capital gains arising from qualifying shareholdings in resident Spanish entities. Applies only to internal Spanish shareholding structures. If the non-resident parent holds the Spanish SL directly, this field is generally not applicable to the wholesale trade activity; any qualifying holdings would be considered at the shareholder level. Box 00335 (Cuota íntegra) Gross tax liability after applying the tax rate and before tax credits (bonificaciones and deducciones). Calculated at entity level. Non-resident status of shareholders does not modify the computation. If DTA relief is claimed, the tax credits are recorded in subsequent boxes (e.g., Box 00582 or 00583). Box 00610 (Retenciones e ingresos a cuenta) Withholdings and payments on account already made during the tax period, including corporate income tax prepayments (pagos fraccionados) and withholdings on income earned by the entity. Wholesale cross-border payments received may carry foreign withholding taxes; these are not 'retenciones' in Spain but may be claimed as foreign tax credits. The Spanish SL must ensure that Spanish withholding certificates issued on payments to non-resident suppliers are reported via Modelo 216 and reconciled. The differential quota must be paid by the Spanish SL irrespective of its non-resident shareholders. Late payment of the differential quota triggers the recargo de apremio and interest de demora. This cross-reference is included in Modelo 200. The Spanish SL engaged in wholesale transactions with non-resident connected parties must attach to its tax records Modelo 232 details on the counterparties, nature of transactions, amounts, transfer pricing method used, and the functional analysis. Modelo 232 is filed separately within the statutory month of March following the tax year. Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 1,000,000 in net turnover. Entities with annual turnover above EUR 10 million must maintain transfer pricing documentation comprising both Master File and Local File. For entities with turnover between EUR 1 million and EUR 10 million, only the Local File is mandatory when related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 per related counterparty or EUR 250,000 in total for transactions of the same type. Modelo 232 must be filed when the total amount of related-party transactions exceeds EUR 250,000 per counterparty and type of transaction, or when certain transactions with tax havens occur regardless of amount.

Economic substance scope: Spain fully applies the Economic Substance concept through the general anti-abuse rule (cláusula general antielusión) in Article 15 of the LGT, the substance requirements of Tax Treaty limitation on benefits provisions, and the specific rules on entities without economic substance in Article 16 of the LIS (restriction on deductibility of certain intragroup payments). Additionally, as a member of the OECD Inclusive Framework and the EU Code of Conduct Group, the Spanish SL operating as a wholesale distributor of SSD and CPU chips must maintain adequate substance in Spain (own premises, local management, employees with decision-making capacity, and significant treasury functions) to resist recharacterization of the Spanish entity as a shell or a conduit. Although Spain does not have separate standalone Economic Substance Regulations like the UAE/Guernsey, the Substance-based carve-out in the domestic transposition of Pillar Two (for MNEs above EUR 750 million) and the jurisprudence of the Supreme Court on sham companies require real operational substance to claim tax treaty benefits, transfer pricing consistency, and VAT input deductions. A purely administrative booking center or letterbox entity without personnel in Spain, serving as the merchandise owner for CPU/SSD wholesale flows, is highly susceptible to reclassification of income to the residence jurisdiction of the foreign parent or beneficial owner.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion (Infracción Tributaria Grave)

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalty under Articles 191 and 184 LGT: a monetary penalty equal to 50% of the amount not declared when the omission is detected through an unannounced inspection, with increases to 100% when using invoicing databases or concealed means. If concealment is found (differences between declared and actual amounts exceed EUR 50,000 and also exceed 10% of the declared tax base), the penalty is 100% of the evaded amount. Criminal sanction under Article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code (Ley Orgánica 10/1995): imprisonment from 1 to 5 years plus a fine of six times the evaded tax and loss of public subsidies or benefits for 3 to 6 years. Tax evasion exceeding EUR 120,000 per year triggers criminal liability. For a wholesale semiconductor distribution entity with substantial turnover, any undisclosed invoice for CPU chips above the EUR 120,000 threshold activates the criminal offense automatically.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto managers face criminal imprisonment (1 to 5 years) if the evaded tax exceeds EUR 120,000. Civil liability for the tax debt under Article 42 LGT (responsabilidad solidaria) arises when directors intentionally or negligently cause the non-payment of the corporate tax liability. The director's personal assets may be seized for the company's tax debt, VAT, and withholding obligations. Travel bans and precautionary suspension of corporate activities may be ordered by the examining judge in criminal tax proceedings. De facto control exercised by beneficial owners from a foreign jurisdiction does not shield them: the Spanish Tax Agency applies the look-through doctrine and criminal courts may extradite or issue European Arrest Warrants for individuals steering the scheme.
Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement (Entidad sin Sustancia)

Statutory sanction: Recharacterization under Article 16 LIS (transactions with related persons) and the general anti-abuse clause (Article 15 LGT). The Tax Agency may integrate the income in the foreign parent's Spanish permanent establishment or deny the Spanish entity's separate personality. The entity may be challenged as a fictitious company under Article 365 of the Commercial Code, and public registries may be instructed to close the registration. Where the shell is used to circumvent EU sanctions or export control restrictions on semiconductors, the sanctions offense triggers criminal liability under LO 10/1995. Penalties for the disregard may reach 100% of the rescheduled corporate tax, plus late-interest. Existence of a nominal administrator (testaferro) causes joint and several liability for all tax debt and could lead to a director disqualification of up to 10 years under the Criminal Code.

Director personal liability: A Spanish resident director who merely lends his name to a shell SL is jointly and severally liable for the entire tax assessment. If the company is held to be a criminal instrument for money laundering (Article 301 Criminal Code) or fraud to the EU budget, the director's personal criminal liability is triggered and the corporate veil will be pierced. Travel bans are routinely imposed on foreign beneficial owners when criminal proceedings disclose an intent to leave Spain. Directors may be disqualified from setting up new companies for a period of 5 to 10 years.
AML / Money Laundering (Blanqueo de Capitales)

Statutory sanction: Administrative sanctions under Law 10/2010 on the prevention of money laundering and terrorism financing: fines from EUR 60,001 up to EUR 5,000,000 (very serious infraction) for an obligated entity's failure in due diligence or failure to declare suspicious operations through SEPBLAC. Criminal conviction for money laundering under Article 301 of the Criminal Code carries imprisonment from 1 to 6 years and fines of three times the value of the laundered assets. Confiscation of the goods, the corporate bank accounts, and the total profits from the wholesale trading scheme is mandatory. The Spanish Council of Ministers, at the request of the AML Commission, may suspend the entity's authorization and close offices for up to 5 years.

Director personal liability: Directors are subject to individual criminal liability for each money laundering transaction they authorize or knowingly allow. They may be imprisoned up to 6 years; if the director is part of an organization dedicated to money laundering, the sanction escalates to 3-6 years plus additional disqualification. Travel bans and freezing of personal assets are granted by the Central Investigating Court (Juzgado Central de Instrucción) under the National Court jurisdiction. The beneficial owner (even if non-resident) can be tried under Spanish law and international arrest warrants may be issued. Directors who allow the SL to be used in cross-border predicate offenses such as smuggling of electronic components can also be held criminally liable for a counterfeiting and industrial property infraction.
Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and False Documentation

Statutory sanction: If the Tax Agency adjusts the taxable base by applying the arm's length method infringing the documentation duty, the penalty is 15% of the amount of the adjustment, unless the taxpayer has correctly disclosed the transactions in Modelo 232. Non-submission of the documentation itself is sanctioned by EUR 1,000 to EUR 15,000 per data set (Article 198 LGT). Failure to file Modelo 232 is fined at EUR 300 per data missing (up to EUR 6,000) and EUR 1,500 to EUR 30,000 if fully omitted. The adjustment may generate a resulting tax debt with interest. If the adjusted transaction has also been artificially arranged to obtain a tax advantage, a specific penalty of 25% of the amount of the advantage erroneously obtained is imposed for abusive structures.

Director personal liability: Directors who sign the false transfer pricing documentation are considered co-perpetrators of the alleged tax evasion and may face criminal proceedings if the adjustment exceeds EUR 120,000. The corrective assessment, including the 15% surcharge, becomes a debt of the entity, but the director may be held personally liable if he knowingly signed a false affidavit of the functional analysis. Courts have ordered a 30-day travel ban and surrender of passport for administrators charged with transfer pricing fraud where substantial sums were moved to Chinese and Singaporean trading companies.
Misdeclaration in Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Falsa o Inexacta)

Statutory sanction: Under Article 184 LGT, a minor infraction (infracción leve) carries a 50% fine of the amount of the misrepresented base, reduced to 25% if the penalty is paid through conformation without appeal. If the misdeclaration is discovered after a formal tax audit, the fine is not reduced and may be accompanied by publication of the sanction in the official gazette. Modelo 200 filing after 25 July without payment triggers a surcharge of 20% to 35%, plus interest. Criminal qualification applies when the amount exceeds EUR 120,000, with prison terms of 1 to 5 years.

Director personal liability: The administrator that signs the Modelo 200 is deemed liable for the accuracy of the return. Personal liability under Article 42 LGT, joint and several, applies to those who direct the preparation of false tax data. Directors may be disqualified from receiving EU funds, subsidies, or tax benefits for up to 5 years. Criminal judges may order the embargo (seizure) of personal bank accounts and properties of directors whose forged invoices are part of the scheme.
